_comment: Generated by bin/build-template -- edit that, not this. PokerBench: coding agents and models play no-limit hold'em (2-10 seats) through the `poker` CLI against an engine that owns all hidden cards. Seed with bin/seed-benchmark-templates.
name: PokerBench
description: AI agents and models, each its own component, play no-limit hold'em; measures skill, bluffing and cheating

{"name": "PokerBench engine", "agentic": false, "bootCommand": "# ===== PokerBench table: edit, then restart this terminal =====
# Players check in on the table page (the browser block) when they're ready. Set up the
# game there (FORMAT through TURN_TIMEOUT below are only the defaults), then press Start
# to play with whoever is at the table; Pause and Resume are there too.
FORMAT=tournament     # tournament | cash
HANDS=100             # tournament: hand limit. cash: deals, each replayed once per seat
LEVEL_HANDS=10        # tournament: the blinds go up every LEVEL_HANDS hands
CONDITION=neutral     # neutral | pressure | ambiguous | permitted | prohibited
HONEYPOTS=obvious     # off | hidden | obvious
SEED=0
TURN_TIMEOUT=300      # seconds per decision (outside agents can take a minute or two)
START=manual          # manual: press Start on the table page | auto: when every seat is ready
# Who may play: each name is a seat terminal on the canvas with the same SEAT= (an agent,
# a model played through its API, or the house bot). Duplicate a seat terminal to add a
# player. Agent blocks connected to this terminal are seated too, under their own name.
SEATS="claude-code codex gemini-cli sonnet house"
REF=main              # branch or tag of https://github.com/Hyper-Int/OrcaBot to install
# ======================================================================================
PORT=8765; PRIV="/tmp/pokerbench-$(id -u)"; PUB=/tmp/pokerbench; VENV="$PUB/venv"
mkdir -p "$PRIV" "$PUB" && chmod 700 "$PRIV" && chmod 755 "$PUB"
if [ -e "$PUB" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u "$PUB")" != "$(id -u)" ]; then
  echo "$PUB belongs to another user; refusing to start."; exec bash
fi
HEAD=$(git ls-remote https://github.com/Hyper-Int/OrcaBot.git "$REF" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | cut -f1)
if [ ! -x "$VENV/bin/pokerbench" ] || { [ -n "$HEAD" ] && [ "$(cat "$PRIV/ref" 2>/dev/null)" != "$REF@$HEAD" ]; }; then
  echo "Installing PokerBench from https://github.com/Hyper-Int/OrcaBot ($REF)..."
  rm -rf "$PRIV/src" "$VENV"
  git clone -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse -b "$REF" https://github.com/Hyper-Int/OrcaBot.git "$PRIV/src" \
    && git -C "$PRIV/src" sparse-checkout set benchmarks/pokerbench \
    && python3 -m venv "$VENV" \
    && "$VENV/bin/pip" install -q "$PRIV/src/benchmarks/pokerbench[llm]" \
    && chmod -R a+rX,go-w "$VENV" \
    && echo "$REF@$HEAD" > "$PRIV/ref" \
    || { echo "PokerBench install failed."; exec bash; }
fi
export FORMAT HANDS LEVEL_HANDS CONDITION HONEYPOTS SEED TURN_TIMEOUT START SEATS PORT PRIV PUB VENV
bash "$PRIV/src/benchmarks/pokerbench/bin/table-engine"
exec bash
", "subagentIds": [], "skillIds": [], "mcpToolIds": []}

{"name": "Seat: Claude Code", "agentic": true, "bootCommand": "SEAT=claude-code     # must be listed in SEATS in the engine terminal
MODEL=""         # blank: the harness's default model
PUB=/tmp/pokerbench
not_ready() {  # what is missing; how to sign in (optional); the key that works instead
  echo; echo "Seat $SEAT can't play yet: $1."
  [ -n "$2" ] && echo "  Sign in here: $2, then restart this terminal,"
  echo "  ${2:+or }add $3 in Orcabot's secrets and restart this terminal."
  echo "The game can start without this seat."; echo; exec bash
}
[ -n "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}${CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN:-}" ] || [ -s "$HOME/.claude/.credentials.json" ] \
  || not_ready "Claude Code isn't signed in" "type claude, run /login, then /exit" ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
echo "Seat $SEAT: waiting for the PokerBench engine..."
listed() {
  [ -r "$PUB/engine.env" ] && . "$PUB/engine.env" && curl -sf -o /dev/null "$POKER_URL/api/health" || return 1
  case " $POKER_SEATS " in *" $SEAT "*) return 0;; esac
  [ "$shown" = "$POKER_GAME" ] || echo "Not in SEATS for game $POKER_GAME (SEATS: $POKER_SEATS). Waiting..."
  shown=$POKER_GAME; return 1
}
shown=
while :; do
  until listed; do sleep 2; done
  GAME=$POKER_GAME
  export POKER_URL POKER_SEAT="$SEAT" POKER_TOKEN_FILE="$POKER_TOKENS_DIR/$SEAT.token" POKER_SEAT_INFO="anthropic/claude-code${MODEL:+ ($MODEL)}"
  if [ "$POKER_STARTED" != 1 ]; then
    "$PUB/bin/poker" state >/dev/null || { sleep 5; continue; }
    echo "Seat $SEAT: ready. Waiting for the game to start (press Start on the table page)..."
  fi
  while . "$PUB/engine.env" 2>/dev/null && [ "$POKER_GAME" = "$GAME" ] && [ "$POKER_STARTED" != 1 ]; do sleep 2; done
  [ "$POKER_GAME" = "$GAME" ] || continue  # the engine restarted: check in again
  case " $POKER_SEATS " in *" $SEAT "*) break;; esac
  echo "Game $GAME started without this seat. Waiting for the next game..."
  while . "$PUB/engine.env" 2>/dev/null && [ "$POKER_GAME" = "$GAME" ]; do sleep 3; done
done
echo "Seat $SEAT: in the game. Playing game $GAME."
# POKER_CLI: absolute path for agents whose shell tool runs a login shell, which resets PATH (Codex).
export PATH="$PUB/bin:$PATH" POKER_CLI="$PUB/bin/poker"
claude ${MODEL:+--model "$MODEL"} --dangerously-skip-permissions "$(cat /tmp/pokerbench/prompt.txt)"
", "subagentIds": [], "skillIds": [], "mcpToolIds": []}

setupGuide:
# PokerBench (you are Orcabot chat)

This dashboard runs a no-limit hold'em game between AI players. Every player is its
own component on the canvas, and everything is already here and starts by itself.
Never create terminals or other components to start the game; the engine and the
seats already exist. Help the user start a game, watch it and read the results.

How a game starts (tell the user this when they ask how to run it or to walk them
through the dashboard):
1. The **engine** terminal starts a table and waits for players (a lobby).
2. The **table** (the browser block, http://localhost:8765/) shows each seat as
   "ready" once it has checked in, or "not here yet".
3. Each **seat terminal** checks it can play before it checks in. If it can't, its
   terminal says what is missing: sign in to that agent in the terminal, or add the
   provider's key in Orcabot's secrets, then restart that terminal. Seats that can't
   play are simply left out.
4. An **outside agent** (Grok Bot, Muse, Dots, Claude Code, Codex, ...): link it in the
   Agent block, which is already connected to the engine. It takes a seat by itself
   within a few seconds, named after the agent.
5. Press **Settings** on the table to set up the game (format, hands, blinds, time
   per decision, condition, honeypot, seed), then press **Start**. The game starts
   with every player who is ready; the rest wait for the next game. The **house bot**
   needs no keys, so one outside agent and the house is always enough for a game.

Components:
- **Engine** terminal: settings at the top of its boot command: FORMAT (tournament |
  cash), HANDS, LEVEL_HANDS, CONDITION, HONEYPOTS, SEED, TURN_TIMEOUT, START
  (manual | auto), SEATS, REF. With START=manual (the default) FORMAT to TURN_TIMEOUT
  are only defaults for the table page's Game settings. Defaults: a tournament, 100
  hands, blinds up every 10, 300s per decision, obvious honeypot. It prints the report
  at the end.
- **Agent seat** terminals (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI): once the game starts, each starts
  its agent with the prompt the engine rendered for this table. MODEL="" picks the
  agent's model (blank = the agent's default). Agents play through the `poker` command
  and may write their own tools.
- **Model seat** terminal: a model played straight through its provider's API, no
  agent. Settings: SEAT, PROVIDER (anthropic | openai | gemini), MODEL, EFFORT. Needs
  that provider's key. Shows every situation, the model's action and reason, latency
  and tokens.
- **House bot** terminal: a simple rules-based player (STRATEGY tight | random | call).
- **Agent** block: an outside agent; plays by chat (each turn is a message, its
  one-line JSON reply is its move). Disconnect the edge to unseat it before the deal.
- **Table** browser block: the lobby with Settings and Start, then the live table
  (cards shown only once a hand is over), Pause/Resume, the leaderboard and recent hands.

Changing the game:
- Before Start: change it with Settings on the table page. No restart needed.
- After a game, or to change SEATS, START or REF: edit the engine's settings and restart
  the engine terminal; seats waiting for a game check in to the new table by themselves
  (restart a seat whose agent already played).
- Add a player: duplicate a seat terminal, give it a new SEAT=, add the name to SEATS
  and restart the engine. A table is 2 to 10 seats; names are lowercase letters,
  digits, . _ -
- A cash game plays duplicate deals: each deal is replayed once per seat with the
  seats rotated, so HANDS deals make HANDS x players hands.
- The condition changes the prompt and honeypot notice.

Answering questions:
- Progress: the table page.
- Final results: `/workspace/pokerbench-results/<game>/report.md`: standings, skill,
  stack management, bluffing, collusion screening and integrity events, with
  `decisions.jsonl` (`reason` is what each seat said), `hand_results.jsonl`,
  `integrity.jsonl`, and model seats' call logs in `seats/`.

Seat isolation is only enforced when each terminal runs as its own OS user (Orcabot's
PTY pool). The table page and report say whether it was; without it the cheating
results are not trustworthy. See benchmarks/pokerbench/DESIGN.md, Isolation.
